## Scope and rule precedence

This review was limited to consistency. The applicable rules were evaluated in this order:
path-specific instructions, topic-specific knowledge, repository-wide guidance, then nearby
compliant precedent. Functional correctness, security, performance, general test adequacy, and
issues caught by CI were excluded unless an explicit consistency rule required review.

## Inventory

### 1. Separate `javaagent-unit-tests` project

- Changed code: `instrumentation/mcp/mcp-java-sdk-0.14/javaagent-unit-tests/build.gradle.kts:1-13`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/kubernetes-client-7.0/javaagent-unit-tests/build.gradle.kts:1-8`
- Frequency: rare
- Disposition: needed
- Applicable rules: the new-module checklist requires all subprojects to be registered and use the
  correct plugin; the closest same-test-type precedent governs project separation.
- Why: the project isolates direct unit tests of javaagent helper classes from agent integration
  tests and follows the established `javaagent-unit-tests` shape.

### 2. Explicit `instrumentation-annotations-support` compile dependency

- Changed code: `instrumentation/mcp/mcp-java-sdk-0.14/javaagent/build.gradle.kts:20`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/reactor/reactor-3.1/javaagent/build.gradle.kts:26-30`
- Frequency: rare among consumers of the Reactor instrumentation library
- Disposition: needed
- Applicable rules: `.github/agents/knowledge/gradle-conventions.md:158-171` rejects unused
  dependencies, while the Java compile classpath must contain types exposed by referenced APIs.
  The demonstrated compile-classpath requirement takes precedence over an apparent unused import
  search.
- Why: removing the dependency makes compilation fail because
  `ReactorAsyncOperationEndStrategy` exposes
  `io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.api.annotation.support.async.AsyncOperationEndStrategy`.
  The dependency is therefore required even though MCP sources do not name that type directly.

### 3. Advice returns an `Object[]` to replace an argument and retain exit state

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/mcp/mcp-java-sdk-0.14/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/mcp/v0_14/McpClientSessionInstrumentation.java:47-65`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/executors/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/executors/JavaExecutorInstrumentation.java:140-154`
- Frequency: rare
- Disposition: needed
- Applicable rules: `.github/agents/knowledge/javaagent-advice-patterns.md` requires static,
  suppressed advice and permits bookkeeping state; the existing `AssignReturned.ToArguments`
  convention governs simultaneous argument replacement and advice state.
- Why: one returned element replaces the immutable MCP request with its metadata-preserving copy,
  while the other carries state to exit advice. The closest compliant pattern uses the same
  multi-value advice return mechanism.

### 4. Public helper boundary for state referenced directly by non-inline advice

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/mcp/mcp-java-sdk-0.14/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/mcp/v0_14/McpToolCallState.java:19-97`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/kubernetes-client-7.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/kubernetesclient/v7_0/CurrentState.java:17-57`
- Frequency: rare
- Disposition: needed
- Applicable rules: `.github/agents/knowledge/general-rules.md:113-126` requires classes and
  members directly referenced by advice to be public; least-access visibility applies only after
  that class-loader boundary rule.
- Why: both advice classes directly call `prepare`, `captureRequestId`, `getRequestParameters`, and
  `finish`. Public visibility is therefore the compliant javaagent helper boundary, while members
  used only by other helpers remain package-private.

### 5. Nested `ThreadLocal` state for cross-method request-ID correlation

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/mcp/mcp-java-sdk-0.14/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/mcp/v0_14/McpToolCallState.java:21-26,29-67,90-99`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/kubernetes-client-7.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/kubernetesclient/v7_0/CurrentState.java:13-41`
- Frequency: rare
- Disposition: unclear
- Applicable rules: repository javaagent precedent permits `ThreadLocal` to bridge distinct
  instrumented methods; generic simplicity guidance disfavors extra state unless its need is
  established. The specific cross-method precedent permits the mechanism, but no explicit
  repository rule establishes the need for the added nested-state chain.
- Why: `sendRequest` and `generateRequestId` are separate hooks, so thread-local correlation is
  established. Preserving `previousState` adds re-entrant nesting support, but the PR does not
  establish whether the SDK can nest these calls. The pattern is compliant and was preserved.

### 6. Volatile request ID populated before asynchronous completion

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/mcp/mcp-java-sdk-0.14/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/mcp/v0_14/McpToolCallRequest.java:11-26`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/kubernetes-client-7.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/kubernetesclient/v7_0/CurrentState.java:20-40`
- Frequency: rare
- Disposition: needed
- Applicable rules: the repository permits mutable cross-method state where lifecycle requires it;
  ordinary immutable request carriers remain preferred when all values are available at creation.
- Why: the SDK generates the JSON-RPC ID after request interception, while span completion can read
  it asynchronously. The mutable field supports the two-phase lifecycle, and `volatile` provides
  visibility across that boundary.

### 7. Lazy Reactor-context span creation and asynchronous end strategy

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/mcp/mcp-java-sdk-0.14/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/mcp/v0_14/McpToolCallMono.java:20-54`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/reactor/reactor-3.4/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/reactor/v3_4/operator/ContextPropagationOperator34Instrumentation.java:51-62`
- Frequency: unique as a combined instrumentation pattern
- Disposition: needed
- Applicable rules: topic-specific Reactor APIs and javaagent invisibility requirements take
  precedence over generic simplicity; singleton naming rules require the runtime strategy
  collaborator to remain lower camel case.
- Why: subscription-time `deferContextual` access is needed to recover the Reactor parent context
  and to avoid starting a span for an unsubscribed publisher. The repository Reactor bridge is the
  closest compliant context-extraction precedent, and the shared end strategy supplies the
  established async success, error, and cancellation lifecycle.

### 8. Explicit failure containment outside advice execution

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/mcp/mcp-java-sdk-0.14/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/mcp/v0_14/McpToolCallMono.java:26-62`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/play/play-mvc/play-mvc-2.4/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/playmvc/v2_4/RequestCompleteCallback.java:27-34`
- Frequency: rare
- Disposition: needed
- Applicable rules: `.github/agents/knowledge/javaagent-advice-patterns.md:292-300` requires
  javaagent instrumentation not to throw; advice-level suppression does not govern code executed
  later by a Reactor callback.
- Why: the callback executes after advice returns, so its nested guards preserve application
  behavior and ensure a span already started is ended if publisher wrapping fails.
